# Same day emergency care spaces

!!! info "Definition"
    A same day emergency care (SDEC) space is a clinical space used to assess, diagnose, monitor and treat patients requiring urgent care without an overnight hospital admission.

## Activity classification

Activity is limited to attendances recorded under department type '5' in the Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS).

## Calculating capacity

#### Pathway: deriving workload

Convert SDEC attendances into occupancy hours using the assumed length of stay.

!!! quote ""

    $$
    \text{Occupancy hours}
    =
    \text{Attendances}
    \times
    \frac{\text{Attendance length of stay (minutes)}}{60}
    $$

#### Operating model: converting workload to capacity

Calculate the required number of SDEC spaces by dividing occupancy hours by the product of the service's annual operational hours and the assumed utilisation rate.

!!! quote ""

    $$
    \text{Required SDEC spaces}
    =
    \frac{\text{Occupancy hours}}
    {\text{Annual operational hours} \times \text{Utilisation rate}}
    $$

## Assumptions

Assumptions may apply to an individual subgroup, several subgroups or all groups.

| Subgroup | Assumption | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All groups | Length of stay | Pathway |
| All groups | Utilisation rate | Operational |
| All groups | Annual operational hours | Operational |


## Notes

* This calculation is based on average demand and an assumed utilisation rate. It may underestimate the capacity required to accommodate peaks in demand.
